ImageDescription.value: Reception lounge at Amantaka luxury resort and hotel at blue hour in Luang Prabang, Laos, with couch and a candle lantern on the low table. Amantaka is one of the 34 properties operated by Aman Resorts, hospitality company founded by Indonesian hotelier Adrian Zecha in 1988, present in more than 20 countries. The hotel, located in a French colonial building, opened in September 2009. A boutique hotel, it contains 24 lavish suites, encircling a central courtyard and is designed with a mixture of traditional Lao furnishings and modern. The suites range in size from 70 to 120 square metres and include eight suites, four pool suites, eight Khan pool suites, two Mekong pool suites and two Amantaka pool suites. All of the rooms have a king-sized bed centre of the suites beneath a traditional high ceiling. They are painted in white and have mahogany or dark wood furnishings and windows. The rooms are reported to be between 1,100 USD and 1,900 USD a night.

ImageDescription.value: The Munich Residenz is a city palace in Munich and was the residence of the Bavarian dukes, electors and kings. Monumental elongated facade in two to three storeys with raised corner pavilions, with a loggia of figures by Ludwig Schwanthaler in front of the central avant-corps; the western section incorporates the previous building (the Kaisersaal wing) from the early 17th century, rebuilt by Leo von Klenze between 1832 and 1842; the eastern pavilion and adjoining rear wing were remodelled for the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
